raw_segments.text: The most abundant mines, either of the precious metals or of the precious stones, could add
little to the wealth of the world.
A produce of which the value is principally derived from its scarcity is necessarily degraded
A service of plate and the other frivolous ornaments of dress and furniture could be
purchased for a smaller quantity of commodities, and in this would consist the sole advantage
which the world could derive from that abundance.
